title: Mahamrityunjaya Mantra Meaning: What the Words Really Say
intro: The Mahamrityunjaya Mantra is chanted for health, protection and peace. Its meaning is gentler and deeper than many people think.

p: Om Tryambakam yajamahe sugandhim pushtivardhanam | Urvarukamiva bandhanan mrityor mukshiya mamritat ||
It comes from the Rig Veda, and is addressed to Shiva as the three-eyed Lord.
We worship the three-eyed one, who is fragrant and nourishes all beings. Like a ripe cucumber is freed from its vine, may he free us from the bondage of death, and not from immortality.
The image is of a fruit that ripens and drops naturally. The prayer asks for release from fear and attachment, not for avoiding life.
It is chanted during illness, before surgeries, on Mondays and on Maha Shivaratri. Many families recite it for elderly parents.
Chanting 108 times with a rudraksha mala is a common practice.
The mantra is meant to calm fear. Chant it as a prayer for strength, along with proper medical care when someone is unwell.

faq.a: No. People chant it for general well-being, protection and peace of mind.

faq.q: How many times should I chant?
faq.a: Many use 108 repetitions, but even a few repetitions with focus are valuable.
